main_result: Claims that Thompson's group F is not amenable. The quantitative form (avg:boundary) says there is a finite S ⊂ F and c_0 > 0 such that every nonempty finite A ⊂ F has max_{h in S} |hA △ A|/|A| ≥ c_0. The argument colours partitions of [0,1] recursively with vectors in the unit ball of L^2([0,1];R^2) via a fixed-point-free Lipschitz map f. An almost-invariant finite A forces the parent colours to be nearly constant in correlation, which contradicts the displacement bound. I checked the algebra of Steps 0–7 and the appendix construction, and found no fatal error. Because the manuscript claims to settle a long-standing open problem, the result should be treated with caution until checked by specialists.
proof_strategy: Fix a Lipschitz map f on the Hilbert ball with uniform displacement δ, and fix parent intervals I_1..I_D and children I_i·I_j. Colour each dyadic partition T recursively: if T respects all parents, colr(T) = f(average of colr(T restricted to I_j)); otherwise 0. For g in F, read off X_I(g) = colr((gT^(n))_I) at one fine level n. Pair transport (dyad:transport) gives an element h of F that moves two separated intervals affinely onto I_1 and I_2 at once, so colours are carried exactly. For a fixed finite A, averaging over A changes each cross-correlation by at most the boundary ratio η, so all separated correlations are within η of one number α. The recursion gives X_{I_i} = f(z_i), and convexity plus Lipschitz continuity then bound E||m - f(m)||^2 by L^2 times a variance that is at most 4/D + 4(1-1/D)η; the α terms cancel. Comparing with δ^2 forces η ≥ c_0 > 0. The tube-and-rotation construction in the appendix gives f itself. I could follow each step, but only by checking constants and the admissibility bookkeeping line by line.
hardest_part: The hardest part to certify is the single-level bookkeeping in Step 0–1 of avg:boundary, namely that admissibility of both g and hg at the same fine level n, together with the normalized-restriction identity from dyad:covariancelemma, really gives the exact colour equality X_I(g) = X_{I_1}(hg) for every g in A. Next is the appendix separation and tube constants (aux:sep, aux:tube, aux:map Step 1c), which I checked but did not re-derive in full detail. I could not independently test the global claim against the literature.

main_result: Claims that Thompson's group F is not amenable (Geoghegan's conjecture). Quantitatively: there is a finite S ⊂ F and c0 > 0 such that for every nonempty finite A ⊂ F, max_{h∈S} |hA△A|/|A| ≥ c0. This contradicts the Følner condition for S. The bound comes from a recursive coloring of dyadic partitions that, via a Lipschitz fixed-point-free map f of the Hilbert unit ball (Benyamini–Sternfeld type, constructed explicitly in the appendix), forces the averaged correlations over A to be nearly constant, which is impossible when the boundary ratio is small. Secondary corollaries on non-unitarizable representations and Bernoulli percolation are stated as consequences of unavailable companion papers and are not part of the proof.
proof_strategy: Fix a Lipschitz map f: B→B with ||f(x)-x|| ≥ δ and a dyadic family of parent intervals I_1..I_D with children I_i·I_j. Define a color colr(T) for each dyadic partition T by a well-founded recursion (apply f to the average of the colors of the restrictions to the parents), and set X_I(g) = colr of the restriction of gT^(n) to I, for a level n chosen fine enough for a given finite A and its translates. Group-theoretic transport lemmas give, for each separated pair of intervals, an element h of F moving them affinely onto I_1 and I_2, so averaged correlations of separated pairs are within the boundary ratio η of a common number α. Exact covariance gives the recursion X_{I_i} = f(z_i), and the pointwise inequality ||m-f(m)||² ≤ L²·avg||z_i-m||² plus the three second-moment bounds yield δ² ≤ L²(4/D + 4(1-1/D)η), so η ≥ c0 > 0. I checked the inequality chain, the restriction/covariance identities, the transport construction, and the appendix construction of f line by line and found no error; the unclear parts are the cited companion results used only in the corollaries.
hardest_part: Whether the single-level admissibility bookkeeping (dyad:eventual(b) applied to A∪SA, then covariance at the same n) and the pair-transport construction are airtight as the definitions are written, since the entire contradiction rests on them. I verified them by hand and they appear correct, but the statement that a short argument of this kind settles a long-open problem (Geoghegan's conjecture, which I believe is open to my knowledge) is exactly the kind of claim that needs an independent expert check that I cannot supply. I also could not check the literature citations.

main_result: Thompson's group F is not amenable (Theorem thm:main). The quantitative form (Proposition avg:boundary): there is a finite S ⊂ F and c0 > 0 such that max_{h∈S} |hA△A|/|A| ≥ c0 for every nonempty finite A ⊂ F. This contradicts the Følner property for S with ε = c0. The argument uses a Lipschitz self-map f of the closed unit ball of infinite-dimensional Hilbert space with uniform displacement δ (Lemma lem:displacement, constructed explicitly in the appendix with δ = 1/2).
proof_strategy: A dyadic coloring recursion assigns to each basic partition T of [0,1] a vector colr(T) in the ball, using f applied to the average of the colors of restrictions of T to D fixed parent intervals. For g in F and a fine level n, the colors X_I(g) of parents and children are defined. A single element h_{I,J} of F transports two separated intervals affinely onto the two fixed parents, so colors are carried exactly across it (covariance lemma). For a finite A, the Følner-type defect η controls all cross-correlations of separated intervals up to a common constant α (Steps 1–2). The recursion X_{I_i} = f(z_i) plus the displacement inequality ‖m − f(m)‖ ≥ δ and Lipschitz continuity gives δ² ≤ L²(4/D + 4(1−1/D)η) after the α-terms cancel (Steps 3–7). I checked each of these inequalities and the constants c0; they are consistent. The construction of f in the appendix (curve γ, tube projection, rotations, map Φ) also appears internally consistent on my reading.
hardest_part: The appendix separation and tube arguments (aux:sep, aux:tube, and the Lipschitz estimate in Step 1 of the proof of aux:map) involve many constants and case splits. I checked the case splits and the constants line by line but did not re-derive every numerical bound independently. The more basic question I could not settle from the text alone is whether a result of this strength (resolving Geoghegan's question about the amenability of F) is correct. The argument I could follow is consistent, but I cannot confirm against the current literature that this is a resolution, and the manuscript itself reports earlier claims in both directions.
